title: Continuous linear retraction onto a finite subextension of the normed algebraic closure
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended absolute value, and finite intermediate fields $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq F\subseteq\Omega$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. There exists a continuous $E$-linear map
$$p_F:\Omega\longrightarrow F,\qquad p_F(a)=a\quad(a\in F),$$
where all fields have their norm topologies. Only linearity and continuity are required: $p_F$ need not be multiplicative, Galois-equivariant, or have operator norm at most one. No completeness of $\Omega$ is assumed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent arithmetic expansion: continuous linear retraction used to detect a finite-field cocycle boundary. WANTED: nonarchimedean Hahn-Banach over the spherically complete local field E; no real/complex Hahn-Banach theorem is invoked.

proof.text: The restriction of the given absolute value to $E$ is its extending $\ell$-adic absolute value by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value]. It is nonarchimedean by that same node, and $E$ is complete by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-complete]. By [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], $0<|\ell|_E=\ell^{-1}<1$. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-proper], every closed ball in $E$ is compact. The absolute value on $\Omega$ is also nonarchimedean: for $x,y\in\Omega$, [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set] puts both in a common finite intermediate field $L$, and [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value] applies to the restriction on $L$. Thus $\Omega$, with $\|x\|=|x|$, is an ultrametric normed $E$-vector space; scalar homogeneity is the multiplicativity of its given absolute value. Restrictions of that absolute value induce exactly the stated topologies on $E$ and $F$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), coefficient-topology expansion: check the scalar and ambient hypotheses Agent expansion; not a proof supplied by the blueprint.

proof.text: Since $E\subseteq F$ are finite intermediate fields, $F$ is finite-dimensional over $E$ by the final assertion of [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. Choose an $E$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ and let $\lambda_i:F\to E$ be its coordinate linear maps, so $a=\sum_{i=1}^d\lambda_i(a)b_i$ for $a\in F$. The norm topology on $F$ makes it a Hausdorff topological $E$-vector space: addition and scalar multiplication are continuous by the norm inequalities and multiplicativity. Since $E$ is complete and nontrivially normed by step 1, [lem-sfb-finite-dimensional-linear-map-continuous] says that every $\lambda_i$ is continuous. The domain topology is the subspace topology from $\Omega$, since both use the same absolute value.

source.place: Paragraph (3), coefficient-topology expansion: continuous finite-field coordinates Agent expansion; not a proof supplied by the blueprint.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-proper-ultrametric-scalar-extension] to $K=E$, $V=\Omega$, $W=F$ and $f=\lambda_i$, separately for each $1\leq i\leq d$. Step 1 verifies nontriviality, the strong triangle inequalities, scalar homogeneity and compactness of every scalar closed ball; step 2 verifies continuity on the induced subspace. Obtain continuous $E$-linear maps $\widetilde\lambda_i:\Omega\to E$ satisfying $\widetilde\lambda_i|_F=\lambda_i$. This extension theorem has no completeness hypothesis on $V$, so none is imposed on $\Omega$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), coefficient-topology expansion: nonarchimedean scalar-functional extension Agent expansion; not a proof supplied by the blueprint.

proof.text: Define $p_F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^d\widetilde\lambda_i(x)b_i\in F$. Each summand is continuous as a map to $F$: it is the composite of the continuous $\widetilde\lambda_i$ with $E\to F$, $c\mapsto cb_i$, whose norm difference is $|b_i||c-c'|$. A finite sum is continuous by the triangle inequality. Additivity and $E$-homogeneity hold termwise. For $a\in F$, step 3 and the basis expansion in step 2 give $p_F(a)=\sum_i\lambda_i(a)b_i=a$. This proves all required clauses; the construction makes no assertion about multiplicativity, Galois equivariance or an operator norm bound.
